title: Prospective Examination on Neurocognitive Outcomes Following Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell (CAR T-Cell) Therapy
summary:
The aim of this clinical study is to gain a better understanding of how CAR-T cell therapy affects mental performance (neurocognition). The study will examine various cognitive functions, such as attention, memory, concentration and thinking ability. The objective is to identify potential changes at an early stage and to better assess how frequently and to what extent such changes occur. The results are intended to help make future treatments safer and to provide more targeted support for affected patients.
The study is designed that CAR-T cell therapy is administered as planned as part of standard medical treatment. The exact course of the therapy, including potential risks and supporting measures, will be explained in detail during the medical consultation. 
The additional examinations as part of this clinical study (such as cognitive tests, i.e. assessments of how the brain or central nervous system processes information; as well as questionnaires, laboratory tests and MRI scans) will be integrated into your regular treatment schedule at specific, pre-determined times. Care will be taken to ensure that these examinations are coordinated as closely as possible with your existing appointments, in order to keep the additional burden on you to a minimum.
conditions: Multiple myeloma and malignant plasma cell neoplasms

interventions.name: The study will follow a structured timeline aligned with the clinical treatment and follow-up course of patients undergoing CAR T-cell therapy. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of hematologic malignancy for which CAR T-cell therapy is indicated

- Scheduled treatment with approved CAR T-cell therapy

- Able to provide informed consent and participate in neurocognitive testing

- German proficiency sufficient to complete validated neuropsychological measures 
(or validated translated tools available)

- Availability for follow-up over a minimum of 6-month post-infusion period
Exclusion criteria:
- Pre-existing moderate to severe neurocognitive impairment (e.g. dementia)

- Active central nervous system (CNS) involvement by disease (e.g. CNS or leptomeningeal infiltration)

- Significant psychiatric conditions (e.g. schizophrenia, severe affective disorder, substance abuse) that may confound cognitive data

- Severe sensory or motor deficits impeding test completion

- Contraindications to MRI examinations as per standard screening guidelines

- Enrollment in other interventional studies
